issues.description: The problem specification and template expect a no-argument milk method messageOnMilk() that returns a String (UML and textual instructions show messageOnMilk():String and example usage in Main calls m.messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository defines the Milkable interface and implementations with a different signature: messageOnMilk(double volume). This parameter mismatch also propagates to Seal and Goat implementations which implement messageOnMilk(double). This structural mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and will prevent them from matching the intended API/behavior described in the problem statement (and expected by the template’s example usage and tests).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Milkable API consistent with the problem statement and template: change the Milkable interface to declare a no-argument method String messageOnMilk(), and update the Seal and Goat classes to implement messageOnMilk() with no parameters, returning the described string ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Alternatively (if the intent was to include a volume), update the problem statement and template (including example usage in Main and the textual description) to document and use messageOnMilk(double volume) and its resulting string format. Preferably align the solution to the existing problem/spec (no-arg messageOnMilk()) so students and tests are not blocked.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) defines the Milkable interface method as messageOnMilk():String and requires the returned text to be "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". The solution repository instead defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (a different method signature) and the Seal/Goat implementations return strings with a volume suffix (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked (1.0L)"). This is a cross-artifact mismatch in the conceptual 'milk' operation: the method signature and the expected return string differ between the problem specification and the reference implementation, which will confuse students about what method to implement and what output to produce.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Milkable API consistent with the problem statement. Either (preferred) change the solution to match the spec: update Milkable to declare String messageOnMilk(); and modify Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning exactly "[AnimalType] [name] is milked" (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked"). Or, if the volume parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and adjust the textual requirement to include the volume suffix so all artifacts match. The first option (align solution to no-arg messageOnMilk()) preserves the stated exercise contract and minimizes student confusion.
